requirement.evidence: Prohibits the use of certain algorithmic rent-setting tools in the local rental market.
requirement.note: The document also covers nonpublic data, the civil action, the lower burden of proof, and the remedies. The card's wording is plainer but consistent with the document.

key_value.evidence: Impacted tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief, up to $1,000 per violation, and attorney’s fees.

effective_date.evidence: Approved on March 3, 2026, this action responds to concerns that some tools use nonpublic market data
effective_date.note: The document gives only the approval date of March 3, 2026. The card adds 30 days under Gov. Code § 36937 to reach 2026-04-02, which assumes March 3 was final adoption. March 3 plus 30 days is April 2, so the arithmetic is right, but the document states no effective date.

status.evidence: The Santa Ana City Council has adopted a new ordinance to strengthen renter protections by limiting the use of certain rent-setting software for residential properties.
status.note: The document presents the ordinance as adopted. The card's computed effective date of April 2, 2026 is before the as-of date of 2026-10-01, so in_force is consistent.

citation.evidence: Approved on March 3, 2026, this action responds to concerns that some tools use nonpublic market data—such as real-time rents, lease activity, and occupancy levels—to influence pricing in ways that may drive rents higher.
citation.note: The card names the ordinance, the March 3, 2026 adoption date, and the missing section numbers, all consistent with the document.
